strategies.overview: Infernape has a unique niche in NU thanks to its phenomenal set diversity and excellent Speed tier. However, it usually opts for two sets, Choice Scarf and Choice Specs, both of which have many upsides. Specifically, Choice Scarf allows Infernape to revenge kill faster Pokemon like Munkidori, Barraskewda, and Kilowattrel, while Choice Specs sets capitalize on Infernape's set ambiguity by unleashing a powerful Overheat or Fire Blast on the physical walls that Choice Scarf Infernape forces in. Additionally, Choice Scarf sets outspeed most other Choice Scarf users, such as Flygon, Munkidori, and Flamigo. However, Infernape faces competition against these exact Choice Scarf users due to them fitting on more teams easily. Additionally, Choice Specs sets can struggle to break through Pokemon like Altaria, Chandelure, and Basculegion-M due to their decent bulk and ability to take both of Infernape's STAB moves comfortably. Infernape also fights for a slot on teams with other Fighting-types, since Toxicroak reliably beats Water-types, Flamigo has access to recovery, Paldean Tauros-W can switch into Incineroar without fear of Knock Off due to being less item reliant than Infernape, and Paldean Tauros-F can easily fit Stone Edge to hit would-be checks like Altaria and Chandelure.
strategies.comments:
Other Options

Infernape can run a Choice Band set, letting it break through defensive tanks like Galarian Slowbro and Overqwil, but it's largely outclassed by other Fighting-types like Flamigo, Toxicroak, and the Paldean Tauros formes. Infernape can run a Swords Dance or Nasty Plot set, making it a excellent setup sweeper; however, it struggles to run all of the moves that it needs and is easily revenge killed by common Choice Scarf users like Munkidori, Chandelure, and Flygon. A lead set of Stealth Rock / Taunt / Endeavor or Encore / Mach Punch or Knock Off with a Focus Sash can be run on hyper offense teams to aid in both setting up and preventing entry hazards. Infernape can run a mixed set of Fire Blast or Overheat / Close Combat / U-turn or Grass Knot or Stone Edge / Knock Off with a Life Orb, allowing it to threaten many walls like Avalugg, Galarian Slowbro, Vaporeon, and Gligar; however, it gets revenge killed by faster foes like Kilowattrel, Munkidori, and Choice Scarf Flamigo, and due to EV constraints, it often is a weaker and worse off wallbreaker than a fully physical or special set.

Checks and Counters

Faster Threats and Priority Users: Barraskewda, Kilowattrel, and Scream Tail can outspeed Infernape and destroy it with their attacks, but none of them enjoy switching into Infernape's STAB attacks. Choice Scarf users such as Flygon, Munkidori, and Chandelure are able to outpace and destroy non-Choice Scarf variants of Infernape. Infernape can be picked off by priority users like Shadow Sneak Decidueye and Aqua Jet Basculegion-M.

Fire-resistant Pokemon: Bulky Water-types like Vaporeon can fairly tank Infernape's attacks and threaten it back with their attacks, but none can repeatedly switch into its Fighting-type attacks. Offensive Water-types like Barraskewda and Paldean Tauros-W can KO Infernape with their attacks, and they can pick it off with Aqua Jet. Chandelure is immune to both of its STAB attacks and easily destroys it; however, Chandelure doesn't enjoy switching directly into Scorching Sands and Knock Off. Basculegion-M can tank Infernape's Fire-type attacks and blank its Fighting-type attacks, but it doesn't enjoy tanking Grass Knot and Knock Off. While Altaria doesn't enjoy switching into Stone Edge variants, it can easily resist both of Infernape's STAB attacks and KO it. Diancie walls Infernape's Fire-type attacks and Choice Specs sets, but it doesn't enjoy switching into Close Combat repeatedly.

Ground-types: Flygon, Rhyperior, and Swampert can easily OHKO Infernape with Earthquake or freely set up entry hazards; however, none of them enjoy directly switching into Infernape's Fighting-type attacks. Gligar is notable for tanking Infernape's physical attacks very well and destroying Infernape with Earthquake, but it can be lured and punished by Choice Specs sets.

movesets.name: Choice Specs
movesets.description:
Set Details

Flamethrower is preferred for its reliability, but Fire Blast is stronger, allowing Infernape to 2HKO foes like Gligar and Munkidori. Overheat allows Infernape to break through common walls like Galarian Slowbro and Gligar; however, Grass Knot offers a coverage move that hits Rhyperior, Swampert, and Basculegion-M super effectively. Focus Blast allows it to 2HKO foes like Porygon2 and Swampert, while Aura Sphere can be used for improved accuracy. Scorching Sands allows it to threaten Chandelure, which otherwise walls it, as well as bulky Poison-types like Galarian Slowbro. Infernape can run Vacuum Wave to pick off weakened targets like Flygon and Inteleon, while Switcheroo can cripple defensive walls like Galarian Slowbro, Altaria, and Bellibolt. U-turn can also be used to ease prediction, allowing Infernape to do some chip damage and bring a partner in against threats like Rhyperior and Diancie. Tera Fire allows Infernape's Fire-type attacks to do major damage on threats like Munkidori and Tornadus while giving it the ability to OHKO foes like Gligar and Galarian Slowbro with Overheat.

Infernape appreciates Grass-types such as Tsareena, Amoonguss, and Decidueye that beat Water- and Ground-types like Vaporeon, Paldean Tauros-W, and Flygon. Infernape pairs nicely with wallbreakers like Substitute Basculegion-M, Flygon, and Toxtricity, since they handle special walls like Vaporeon, Diancie, and Milotic. Psychic- and Ghost-types like Munkidori, Galarian Slowbro, Scream Tail, Chandelure, and Basculegion-M can easily KO Infernape; thus, Dark-types like Overqwil, Incineroar, Scrafty, and Wo-Chien make for good partners, as they can easily handle them. Infernape appreciates entry hazard removers like Altaria and Tsareena, as they allow it to not be worn down by hazards, though they are not outright necessary because Infernape can intentionally use hazards to lower its HP into Blaze range. Due to Altaria, Basculegion-M, and Chandelure resisting or being immune to both of Infernape's STAB attacks, Infernape requires teammates that can threaten them like Sylveon, Toxtricity, and Diancie, respectively. Choice Scarf users like Flygon, Munkidori, and Flamigo can easily revenge kill Infernape, so it partners with switch-ins like Bronzong, Rhyperior, and Bellibolt to handle them. Pivots like Flygon, Munkidori, and Bellibolt pair well with Infernape, since they can draw in Steel-types like Copperajah and Bronzong.

movesets.name: Choice Scarf
movesets.description:
Set Details

U-turn gives Infernape the ability to pivot while letting it chip down defensive tanks like Galarian Slowbro, Swampert, and Porygon2. Knock Off allows it to pressure foes like Rhyperior and Kilowattrel that rely on their items, as well as hitting both Chandelure and Basculegion-M, while Stone Edge allows Infernape to beat Chandelure as well as Flying-types like Altaria, Galarian Articuno, and Tornadus. Switcheroo lets it cripple defensive tanks like Amoonguss, Bellibolt, and Vaporeon. Infernape can use Thunder Punch alongside Iron Fist, letting it threaten Water- and Flying-types like Barraskewda, Basculegion-M, and Flamigo. Tera Fighting enables Infernape to threaten a 2HKO on Diancie and Flygon with Close Combat. Tera Dark allows Infernape to tank Psychic- and Ghost-type attacks from Munkidori, Uxie, Chandelure, Decidueye, and Brambleghast.

Choice Scarf Infernape often draws in Fighting-resistant foes like Galarian Slowbro, Gligar, and Sylveon, so it best partners with Toxtricity, Barraskewda, and Munkidori to check these switch-ins. Infernape can form a VoltTurn core with other pivots like Kilowattrel, Flygon, and Barraskewda, since they can pressure defensive tanks like Vaporeon, Diancie, and Amoonguss. Additionally, they bring in foes like Bronzong and Amoonguss that Infernape can take advantage of. Bulky Water-types like Vaporeon and Swampert can act as blanket checks to its attacks and threaten Infernape back with their STAB attacks; thus, it pairs with Grass-types like Decidueye, Amoonguss, and Tsareena to check them. Steel- and Dark-types like Bronzong, Klefki, and Overqwil are great partners for Infernape, since they can beat Psychic-types like Munkidori, Uxie, and Galarian Articuno. Entry hazard removers like Altaria, Cramorant, and Tsareena allow Infernape to continuously switch in without getting worn down by hazards.

strategies.overview: Infernape is a flexible Pokemon capable of performing a variety of different roles, taking advantage of its high Speed and equal ability to hit with physical or special attacks. This unpredictability can create opportunities, as its different sets have different checks: For example, Hippowdon is a perfect answer to Close Combat, but it gets toasted by Fire Blast. Infernape has a deep movepool with strong coverage options like Grass Knot, Earthquake, and Gunk Shot as well as great utility moves like U-turn, Knock Off, and Encore. With both Nasty Plot and Swords Dance, it can boost its damage no matter which attacks it uses, and it has STAB priority moves on both sides with Vacuum Wave and Mach Punch. However, despite the many roles Infernape can fill, there are often other Pokemon that can perform better in them. Crucial Pokemon like Amoonguss and Empoleon can survive Infernape's attacks, and support from entry hazards or resources like Terastallization is often necessary to facilitate its task. As a special attacker, its power is overshadowed by fellow Fire-types Armarouge and Volcanion, while Terrakion, Galarian Zapdos, and Mienshao often outperform as Fighting-type wallbreakers. In addition, Infernape's incredible frailty makes it difficult for it to survive against the powerful attacks in the tier, from Gengar's Shadow Ball to Jirachi's Psychic Noise, resulting in very few opportunities to switch in or set up. Infernape also suffers heavily from four-moveslot syndrome: despite its plethora of options it is impossible to fit all of them, and all of its sets will have holes that the opponent can take advantage of.
strategies.comments:
Other Options

Choice Specs with Tera Fire Overheat allows Infernape to OHKO Reuniclus and offensive Empoleon. Add in the power boost from Blaze, and it also KOes Pokemon like Noivern. Infernape's special sets can use Aura Sphere or Focus Blast as an alternative Fighting-type STAB option, with the drawback of underwhelming power or low accuracy respectively. Swords Dance allows Infernape to force its way through its checks. Knock Off can be used on physical sets to hit Psychic-types like Slowbro and Reuniclus, and it can provide utility to the team with its item removing properties. Mach Punch is a priority option for physical sets that can be improved by Infernape's Iron Fist ability. Encore can grant Infernape more opportunities to set up by locking foes into ineffective moves. Infernape can be used as a lead on hyper offense teams with its ability to set Stealth Rock and threaten hazard removers like Cyclizar. Infernape can also run a mixed attacker set, which will typically be specially biased with Close Combat to hit special walls like Umbreon and Hisuian Goodra.

Checks and Counters

Fire-types: None of Infernape's sets have reliable options to answer Fire-types like Armarouge, Entei, and Talonflame. While Infernape can use niche moves like Stone Edge to hit them, using the moveslot for this will likely leave it lacking elsewhere.

Flying-types: Flying-types like Noivern and Talonflame are able to easily tank Infernape's attacks and recover, then OHKO it.

Walls: Slowbro, Hippowdon, and Gastrodon are some of the bulkiest walls in the tier, and they can easily wall physical Infernape and either heal, KO it, or afflict it with status effects. Hisuian Goodra and Umbreon, despite their weakness to Fighting, can cleanly wall Infernape's special sets.

Priority: Priority attackers like Extreme Speed Entei, Accelerock Lycanroc-D, and Aqua Jet Crawdaunt and Barraskewda threaten huge damage on Infernape.

movesets.name: Nasty Plot
movesets.description:
While its power is lower than its Fire-type competition in Armarouge and Volcanion, Nasty Plot Infernape offers immediate speed, faster setup, and access to priority while still posing a threat to much of the metagame. Grass Knot is used to hit Water-types such as Basculegion-F, Slowbro, and Suicune. Vacuum Wave hits Cyclizar, Lycanroc-D, and Crawdaunt, which outspeed or OHKO Infernape with Aqua Jet. Air Balloon allows Infernape to safely set up against Ground-types like Hippowdon and Krookodile. Expert Belt can push some damage thresholds, allowing an unboosted Fire Blast to OHKO Jirachi and a +2 Grass Knot to OHKO Suicune. Tera Fighting lets Vacuum Wave OHKO potential revenge killers Barraskewda, Krookodile, and Terrakion after a Nasty Plot. In combination with Expert Belt and entry hazards, Tera Fighting Vacuum Wave is also able to OHKO Assault Vest Cyclizar. Tera Grass gives Infernape resistances to Water and Ground, allowing it to set up against Pokemon such as Empoleon and Gastrodon, and lets Grass Knot OHKO Hippowdon without a boost and OHKO Gyarados at +2. Tera Fairy lets Infernape set up against Fighting-type attackers like Mienshao and Terrakion.

Nasty Plot Infernape fits best on offense or bulky offense teams looking for a fast Fire-type attacker and setup sweeper. It notably struggles with some of the special walls in the tier like Hisuian Goodra and Umbreon, so it appreciates stronger Fighting- and Fairy-types like Galarian Zapdos and Gardevoir to help chip them into range of Infernape's attacks. Pivot support is important to get the frail Infernape onto the field safely, with teammates like Noivern, Galarian Zapdos, and Cyclizar being able to do so and inviting in Pokemon that Infernape can beat like Jirachi, Slowbro, and Hippowdon. Entry hazards set by Krookodile, Chesnaught, and Kleavor are able to weaken the Pokemon that Infernape is unable to OHKO at +2, like Empoleon and Slowbro. Knock Off support from Mamoswine, Krookodile, and Galarian Zapdos can remove items such as Heavy-Duty Boots and Assault Vest, which can enable Infernape to clean late-game once the opposing team is worn down. Teammates like Stone Edge Lycanroc-D and Meteor Beam Necrozma are valuable in hitting the Fire-types, like Armarouge and Entei, that Nasty Plot Infernape struggles to hit.

movesets.name: Choice Scarf
movesets.description:
Set Details

Choice Scarf Infernape is capable of outspeeding most other Choice Scarf users in the tier, like Krookodile and Galarian Zapdos, making use of its strong STAB moves and ability to pivot. Switcheroo allows Infernape to cripple physical walls like Hippowdon and Slowbro. U-turn allows it to pivot out of poorer matchups into teammates that can take a hit or threaten whatever switches in on Infernape. While the recoil of a Blaze-boosted Flare Blitz will likely KO Infernape, it also empowers the move to OHKO Amoonguss, Wo-Chien, and Jirachi. Tera Fighting lets Close Combat OHKO Krookodile after Intimidate and Umbreon.

Choice Scarf Infernape is an ideal pick for balance teams that need a fast Fire-type that can pivot, revenge kill, and serve as a late-game cleaner that most other Choice Scarf users cannot outspeed. Entry hazard removal from allies like Cyclizar and Noivern is crucial for Infernape as it wants to enter the field often, and it needs as much help as it can get in order to both survive attacks and Rocky Helmet. Infernape's unique ability to invite physical walls like Hippowdon and Slowbro in and cripple them with Switcheroo makes it a great partner for other physical attackers like Krookodile, Rhyperior, and Terrakion. Infernape can be a potent part of a VoltTurn core with partners like Raikou, Basculegion-F, and Magnezone that can threaten physical walls like Hippowdon and Slowbro. Infernape needs bulky allies like Chesnaught, Umbreon, and Jirachi to take attacks for it, often in the form of priority Aqua Jet from Barraskewda and Crawdaunt or Extreme Speed from Entei.

strategies.outdated: This analysis was uploaded prior to The Indigo Disk release and may contain outdated information.
strategies.comments:
Other Options

Fire

Thunder Punch and Knock Off are other options Infernape can choose to run over Close Combat or Flare Blitz. Thunder Punch allows Infernape to threaten several bulky Water-types. It can 2HKO mixed defensive Toxapex most of the time and OHKO Pelipper and Gyarados. With Knock Off, Infernape can not only threaten Ghost-types, such as Skeledirge, but it can also remove key items, such as Heavy-Duty Boots and Eviolite, from the likes of Pelipper, Toxapex, and Porygon2 to make it easier to wear these walls down. However, Close Combat is generally more useful due to the amount of targets it can remove like Ursaluna and Ting-Lu, benefiting Fire teams. Fire Punch can be run over Flare Blitz. Although weaker, using Fire Punch doesn't result in Infernape taking recoil damage, improving its longevity. However, Flare Blitz is more reliable despite its recoil damage, and the recoil damage can be solved when running Ninetales thanks to the its access to Healing Wish. Choice Scarf is another option for Infernape, as this can allow it to outspeed and threaten would-be faster Pokemon, such as Flutter Mane, but this trades away its ability to win one-on-one against more bulky Pokemon like Ursaluna.

movesets.name: Choice Band (Fire)
movesets.description:
Infernape is a great wallbreaker and cleaner on Fire teams. Its Fighting typing grants Infernape and Fire teams a better matchup against Dark teams, being able to threaten the likes of Hydreigon and Greninja while also resisting Bisharp's Sucker Punch, and with Flare Blitz, it can threaten Landorus. Close Combat is Infernape's primary Fighting-type STAB move, massively threaten the likes of Ursaluna and Kyurem. With U-turn, Infernape can safely pivot out of its switch-ins, such as Dondozo, into a teammate that can threaten them. Infernape is also able to serve as a great revenge killer thanks to its access to an Iron Fist-boosted Mach Punch, being able to pick off weakened threats such as Roaring Moon, Iron Treads, and Darkrai.

Ninetales and Torkoal make for great partners for Infernape, as the two of them up sun to further boost Infernape's Flare Blitz. Ninetales also commonly uses Solar Beam, allowing it to OHKO threats to Infernape, such as physically defensive Quagsire, and can heal Infernape with Healing Wish, while Torkoal can remove entry hazards for Infernape with its access to Rapid Spin. Torkoal and Heatran can set Stealth Rock in order to wear down foes for Infernape to pick off. For example, Infernape is guaranteed a 2HKO on Galarian Weezing after Stealth Rock damage. In return, Infernape can OHKO Landorus with Flare Blitz under sun as well as both Ursaluna and Mamoswine without sun. Cinderace is another noteworthy teammate, as not only can it remove hazards with Court Change, but it is also able to revenge kill faster Ghost-types Infernape cannot such as Dragapult and Speed-boosted Ceruledge with Sucker Punch. In return, Infernape's Fighting-type STAB move frees up a moveslot for Cinderace, as the latter no longer needs High Jump Kick. Volcanion is another great teammate, as it provides Fire teams an immunity to Water, and in return, Infernape is able to threaten the likes of Iron Treads and Landorus for it. Talonflame and Moltres provide a Ground immunity, Will-O-Wisp support, and they can bring Infernape in via U-turn. The two of them are also able to lure bulky Pokemon like Ursaluna-B and Ting-Lu for Infernape to break. Talonflame also provides Defog support, while Moltres's bulk allows it to take on Dragonite, which Infernape greatly appreciates. Infernape's wallbreaking enables other wallbreakers and sweepers such as Ogerpon-H, Volcarona, and Ceruledge to clean late-game. In particular, Infernape can remove Alolan Muk and Heatran to enable a sweep from Volcarona.

strategies.overview:
Draft Order: Round 5 onwards

Price Range: 8-9 points

Overview: Infernape is a fast, versatile Pokemon that supplements a draft's offensive options. Infernape is a solid offensive Pokemon due to its coverage, amazing offensive STAB types, good Speed tier, and priority options. It also can provide utility and serve as a fast pivot to bring in its teammates. However, Infernape suffers strongly from four-moveslot syndrome, which limits its potential. Infernape is also frail, leaving it vulnerable to faster, stronger attackers. Further, Infernape's offensive stats are pretty average, making it overly reliant on team support, setup, or damage-boosting items. This makes it better suited as a supplementary offensive option.
strategies.comments:
Common Roles

Revenge Killer: When equipped with a Choice Scarf, Infernape can utilize its amazing Speed tier, powerful STAB moves, and wide array of coverage moves to revenge kill opposing threats. It can also do this on non-Choice Scarf sets, thanks to its access to priority moves like Mach Punch and Vacuum Wave.

Wallbreaker: When equipped with a damage-boosting item like Choice Band, Choice Specs, or Life Orb, Infernape can be an effective wallbreaker with the ability to hit both physically and specially with powerful STAB moves and coverage options.

Setup Sweeper: Access to both physical and special setup moves in Swords Dance and Nasty Plot allows Infernape to be a scary setup sweeper. It also has the option to run a bulkier setup set, thanks to Bulk Up and Calm Mind. These sets are further complemented by priority moves in Mach Punch and Vacuum Wave, enabling Infernape to pick off faster threats or opposing Pokemon with priority of their own.

Sacrificial Lead: Infernape can set up Stealth Rock to help support the team. Access to Taunt also allows it to prevent opposing entry hazards from being set. Endeavor is usually run on this set along with a Focus Sash to allow Infernape to bring an opposing Pokemon to 1 HP.

Common Moves

Primary STAB Moves: Close Combat, Drain Punch, Fire Punch, Flare Blitz, Mach Punch, Aura Sphere, Fire Blast, Flamethrower, Focus Blast, Overheat, Vacuum Wave

Setup Moves: Swords Dance, Nasty Plot, Calm Mind, Bulk Up, Flame Charge, Agility

Utility Moves: Knock Off, U-turn, Stealth Rock, Will-O-Wisp, Taunt, Encore, Switcheroo, Slack Off

Coverage: Earthquake, Grass Knot, Gunk Shot, Rock Slide, Scorching Sands, Stone Edge, Thunder Punch, Zen Headbutt

Niche Moves

Raging Fury: This is used as an alternative to Flare Blitz to avoid recoil damage.

Fling: Infernape can hold a Big Nugget to have a 130 Base Power Dark-type move to hit bulky Psychic- and Ghost-types.

Endure: Infernape can run Endure in conjunction with a Salac Berry to boost its Speed. This is usually run on setup sets that are not able to fit a priority move or Flame Charge. This also has the benefit of activating Blaze to further boost Infernape's damage output. A Custap Berry can also be used with Endure to get an Endeavor off or to deal damage to a faster opposing Pokemon.

Upper Hand: Infernape can run Upper Hand to deal with opposing priority attacks, like Jet Punch from Palafin.

Endeavor: This is used on sacrificial lead sets to severely chip an opposing Pokemon.

Common Items

Choice Scarf: Choice Scarf allows Infernape to revenge kill faster Pokemon or slower ones at +1 Speed. A physical set is usually preferred when running Choice Scarf, thanks to Infernape having powerful and reliable STAB moves in Flare Blitz and Close Combat.

Damage-boosting Items: Infernape makes excellent use of several damage-boosting items. It can equip Choice Band to deal maximum damage on physical sets and Choice Specs on special sets. Life Orb is used to deal maximum damage while still being able to switch up moves. Expert Belt is preferred when Infernape is able to hit most of the opposing team super effectively. Further, Infernape can also make use of Charcoal and Black Belt to boost the power of its STAB moves.

Focus Sash: Focus Sash is used on the sacrificial lead set to allow Infernape to survive any hit as it sets up Stealth Rock. Once the Focus Sash is consumed, Infernape can then use Endeavor to bring an opposing Pokemon down to 1 HP.

Heavy-Duty Boots: Infernape is rather frail and vulnerable to every form of entry hazard, which cuts into its longevity. Heavy-Duty Boots prevents hazards from weakening Infernape.

Niche Items

Resistance Berries: In a pinch, resistance Berries such as Shuca Berry and Passho Berry can allow Infernape to unexpectedly survive an attack, gaining an extra turn to set up or damage a foe.

Weakness Policy: Weakness Policy can be used in conjunction with Calm Mind or Bulk Up on a bulkier set to allow Infernape to beat its checks more easily. It can also be run with Sunny Day, which weakens super effective Water-type attacks and makes them activate Weakness Policy.

Rocky Helmet: Infernape's typing does well defensively into Bug-, Dark-, and Ice-type attacks. Thus, Rocky Helmet can be used to switch in and punish Pokemon that run resisted moves like Knock Off, U-turn, and Ice Spinner. Additionally, Infernape has access to Will-O-Wisp and a reliable recovery move in Slack Off, making it an excellent defensive response to Pokemon like Weavile and Scizor.

Salac Berry: Salac Berry can be used with Endure to give Infernape a Speed boost. This is usually run on special setup sets where a boost in Speed is preferred over Vacuum Wave. Thanks to Blaze, the activation of a Salac Berry also boosts Infernape's Fire-type attacks.

Power Herb: Power Herb allows the charging turn of Solar Beam to be skipped, giving Infernape a powerful option to deal with opposing Water-types like Slowking and Rotom-W attempting to check it.

Clear Amulet: Clear Amulet can be used in niche scenarios to prevent Pokemon with Intimidate like Landorus-T and Qwilfish from dropping Infernape's Attack.

Protective Pads / Punching Glove: Protective Pads can be useful to avoid contact against Rocky Helmet users or Pokemon with Static. This allows Infernape to pivot freely without being punished. Punching Glove is preferred if Infernape is running punching moves like Drain Punch and Thunder Punch.

Tera

Infernape should not be drafted with the intention of making it a Tera Captain, as there is a wide array of more effective higher-tiered Tera Captains. An excellent offensive typing with powerful STAB moves and amazing coverage options enables Infernape to be threatening without needing to be a Tera Captain. However, if chosen to be a Tera Captain, Infernape can utilize Tera Fire or Tera Fighting to further boost the damage from its STAB moves. Additionally, it can use Tera Grass to deal with Water- and Ground-types or Tera Steel to remove its weakness to Psychic- and Flying-types.

Draft Strategy

Infernape works best as a supporting offensive piece in a draft; it should not be the primary offensive option on a draft. Infernape is able to support its teammates in a variety of ways, thanks to its offensive versatility. It is a reliable Choice Scarf user, an excellent pivoting option, and a potent wallbreaker both physically and specially.

Entry Hazards: Even though it has access to Stealth Rock, Infernape appreciates entry hazard support from Pokemon like Great Tusk and Hisuian Samurott to get crucial chip damage on Pokemon to enable Infernape to revenge kill them more easily. It also appreciates strong hazard removal, as it is vulnerable to entry hazards, which severely cut down on how often it can switch in.

Strong Offensive Pokemon: Infernape works best when paired with offensive behemoths like Latios, Darkrai, and Ogerpon-W, which appreciate the pivoting and revenge killing options provided by it.

Faster Pokemon: While Infernape has a solid Speed tier, it is still vulnerable to faster Choice Scarf users. Having faster teammates like Greninja and Meowscarada also enables Infernape to make the most of its versatility rather than being reduced to a revenge killer.

Pivot Options: As Infernape is quite frail and struggles to switch in safely, pairing it with Pokemon that have access to slow pivoting moves like Rotom-W, Galarian Slowking, and Scizor is recommended. This forms a potent VoltTurn core and enables Infernape to hit the field safely.

Checks and Counters

Bulky Water-types: Bulky Water-types like Rotom-W, Slowbro, and Swampert can take a hit from Infernape and threaten to OHKO it with their STAB moves. They have to be wary of coverage moves, though.

Bulky Flying-types: Bulky Flying-types like Zapdos, Dragonite, and Salamence can switch into Infernape and heal any damage with Roost. However, getting their Heavy-Duty Boots removed by Knock Off will limit their longevity if entry hazards are up, and they also have to be cautious of Stone Edge.

Faster Pokemon: Faster Pokemon like Latios and Iron Valiant can outspeed Infernape and OHKO it. It can also easily get revenge killed by Choice Scarf users, especially if it is not holding a Choice Scarf itself.

Priority Moves: Infernape is weak to Water-type priority moves like Jet Punch from Palafin and Aqua Jet from Quaquaval. Infernape's fraility and vulnerability to every form of entry hazard also leaves it prone to being knocked out by strong, neutral priority moves like Extreme Speed from Dragonite and Vacuum Wave from Iron Valiant. Infernape does have the option to run Upper Hand to force mind games but struggles to find room to run it.

Residual Damage: Due to Life Orb and Flare Blitz's recoil alongside Infernape's susceptibility to every form of entry hazard, it often struggles to maintain longevity throughout a match.
